body: hmmm, would it have to do with the .mjs extension of `/_nuxt/entry-521b7af6.mjs` (last `<script>` in `<body>`)

> would it have to do with the .mjs extension

That does ring a bell. yes 🤔 I think someone else reported a similar problem on discord a few days ago (so it's good we now have an issue for it).

aha! this here. the filename matches an extension (`.mjs`), but doesn't match any specific one, so it gets the default `text/html`

https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/blob/c8667f9ff75275b1c8743411cc996aac032434f2/core/tauri-runtime/src/http/mime_type.rs#L60

I could attempt a PR on this to add .mjs (and maybe some other extensions and mime types?), but I want to make sure that this is what tauri wants first. Also, I'm not sure, but is .mjs a standardised JavaScript file extension? Because if it isn't, it may be better to change on the nuxt side instead

edit: .mjs is at least recognised as a common file extension if not a standardised one, as per [here (link from a comment in the file, just one line below, heh)](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Basics_of_HTTP/MIME_types/Common_types)

If webkit is able to handle .mjs files i don't see a reason not to add support for it. Buuut i remember that we talked about this a while back, so i wonder why we didn't add it 🤔 

> I could attempt a PR on this to add .mjs

Sure, we always appreciate PRs!

> and maybe some other extensions and mime types?

Hmm, i don't think that's necessary, since the `infer` crate should be able to handle most of what we need (plus the uri match function should be relatively extensive fallback-wise). If you know of another _common_ extension that isn't working then don't mind me.

> Also, I'm not sure, but is .mjs a standardised JavaScript file extension? Because if it isn't, it may be better to change on the nuxt side instead

If nuxt outputs it by default i can't imagine that it's not standard-ish.

> If webkit is able to handle .mjs files i don't see a reason not to add support for it

Hmm I think it's just the file extension/mime type that is the issue here, it is just javascript after all :p

> since the `infer` crate should be able to handle most of what we need

ahh right, this makes more sense now that I look at the code more

and alright, I'll look into making a PR then!

issue.title: [feat] Handle or warn when the user's public base path is not empty

repository.name: tauri
repository.description: Build smaller, faster, and more secure desktop and mobile applications with a web frontend.

issue.body:
### Describe the problem

When using vite, the user may define a [public base path](https://v2.vitejs.dev/guide/build#public-base-path) that is prepended the the url where the app is served in `dev` or in `preview`. 

When a custom base path is specified in `vite.config.ts`, `npm run tauri dev` works as expected, but `npm run tauri build` just shows a white screen. Upon enabling developer tools on the build, you see that the webview is complaining about MIME types of css and javascript files. So though this looks at first like a MIME type issue, I think it's just that the webview is looking for the js and css at the wrong path. 



### Describe the solution you'd like

Its possible this is all expected behavior. But for me as a newcomer, it led to a bug that took a long time to diagnose. 

Perhaps tauri could be updated to handle non-empty public base paths. Or warning messages could be added somewhere for diagnosing this. It's possible [other people have had the same issue](https://github.com/tauri-apps/tauri/issues/4098#issuecomment-1194715084). 

For anyone else searching base on error messages:
In the webview devtools console I was seeing: `TypeError: 'text/html' is not a valid JavaScript MIME type.` and `Did not parse stylesheet at 'tauri://localhost/<custom_base_path>/assets/index-D5V9wA_-.css' because non CSS MIME types are not allowed in strict mode.`

And my solution was to comment out the `base:` option in `defineConfig()` in `vite.config.ts`
